section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Usual Notion of Convergence
section_1.content: Briefly revisit the Euclidean metric (standard distance). Explain that in the real number line, a sum converges if the 'tail' of the sequence gets arbitrarily close to zero in magnitude. Visualize this as a point moving closer and closer to a destination on a line.
section_1.example: Visualizing the geometric series 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8... as a hiker approaching a signpost 1 mile away.

section_2.title: Introducing the 2-adic Metric
section_2.content: Define the 2-adic valuation: a number is 'small' if it is divisible by high powers of 2. Introduce the 2-adic distance: |x - y|_2 = 2^(-v_2(x-y)). Explain that higher powers of 2 make points 'closer'.
section_2.example: A digital robot that considers two numbers 'close' if their binary representations share many common digits starting from the right (the least significant bit).

section_3.title: Paradoxical Convergence
section_3.content: Demonstrate the core concept: the infinite sum 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... converges in the 2-adic metric. Contrast this with the real number line, where this sum clearly diverges to infinity.
section_3.example: An animation showing 2^n getting smaller in 2-adic space, collapsing toward -1, while in standard space it shoots off to the edge of the screen.

section_4.title: Visualizing the 2-adic Ultrametric Property
section_4.content: Introduce the Strong Triangle Inequality: |x + y|_2 ≤ max(|x|_2, |y|_2). This defines a 'non-Archimedean' space. Visualize this as a fractal-like tree structure (the Cantor set or p-adic tree) where every point is either identical or completely separate.
section_4.example: A 'bouncing ball' analogy where the ball can only jump to positions that are powers of 2, landing in 'nested buckets' rather than sliding along a flat floor.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Synthesize the two worlds: Real numbers measure size by 'magnitude', while p-adic numbers measure size by 'divisibility'. Highlight how this shifts our understanding of what it means for an infinite series to 'settle down'.
section_5.example: A split-screen comparison: A mountain climber (Real) vs. a code-breaker (2-adic) analyzing the same sequence of numbers.
